newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mobutu calls rebel leader a patriot, urges peace.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu calls rebel leader a patriot, urges peace.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko was quoted on Sunday as describing the man who wants to topple him as a "nationalist patriot".

In an interview published by the South African Sunday Times and conducted at his presidential residence in Kinshasa a few days ago, Mobutu urged rebel leader Laurent Kabila to come to the negotiating table and make peace.

"Kabila is a nationalist patriot. I urge him to come to the table with his Zairean brothers and sisters to restore peace in the country and to contribute to the achievement of the current democratic process," Mobutu told the newspaper.
Mobutu has been in power for 32 years and is reputed to have amassed a vast personal fortune while his country sank into economic chaos, rampant poverty and now political disarray.
Peace talks began on Sunday at a secret location in South Africa.

But there appears to be little prospect of a ceasefire in the six-month civil war or compromise from Kabila's rebels who have captured over a third of the country with little opposition from a demoralised government army.
"My objective has three points," Mobutu was quoted as saying in written replies to questions put by the newspaper.
"To safeguard unity and peace between all sons and daughters of Zaire, to preserve territorial integrity, and to make Zaire a modern democracy."
Mobutu said his idea was to get all Zairean protagonists around the table to reach an agreement on these issues.
But Kabila is adamant that Mobutu himself is the problem and must finally relinquish power.

Asked if he agreed with the perception that Zaire needed change, Mobutu replied: "I am the person who opened up the way to what some call political adjustments or the democratisation process. I believe the democratisation process should not be infringed."
